items.title: Vulnerabilities in Node.js and Brotli Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
items.summary: On October 21, 2026, Node.js announced the availability of fixes for multiple vulnerabilities across the following supported release lines: 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x.  These vulnerabilities impact critical operations such as the Brotli decoder, DNS resolution, and TLS certificate validation. The vulnerabilities pose risks for remote code execution and traffic interception. For more information, see Node.js Security Release .  The following vulnerabilities have a Security Impact Rating (SIR) of High and are addressed in this advisory: CVE-2026-111497 - Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write; p

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.summary: Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, a critical security compromise involving Certificate Authorities that are managed by  eMudhra was uncovered. A security researcher demonstrated that the private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an unprecedented error in their Key Generation Ceremony (KGC) in April 2025. This allows anyone to brute-force acquire these private keys within seconds. items.title: Cisco Identity Services Engine Authorization Bypass Vulnerability
items.summary: A vulnerability in the authorization mechanism of Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) and Cisco ISE Passive Identity Connector (ISE-PIC) could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to obtain an endpoint identity certificate. This vulnerability is due to improper authorization checks. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to bypass authorization to obtain an endpoint certificate. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. items.title: Cisco Unified Communications Manager Cross-Site Scripting Vulnerability
items.summary: A vulnerability in the web-based management interface of Cisco Unified Communications Manager (Unified CM) and Cisco Unified Communications Manager Session Management Edition (Unified CM SME) could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to conduct a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack against a user of the interface. This vulnerability exists because the web-based management interface does not properly validate user-supplied input. items.title: Cisco UCS Central Software Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.summary: A vulnerability in the web-based management interface of Cisco UCS Central Software could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to achieve remote code execution or conduct information disclosure attacks on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input in an HTTP request. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected endpoint on an affected device. items.summary: A vulnerability in Cisco Expressway Series could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to obtain sensitive information from an affected device. This vulnerability is due to insufficient authorization checks of HTTP requests during Mobile and Remote Access (MRA) provisioning. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted URL request to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to access sensitive information that they would otherwise not have authorization to access. items.title: Open Source Snort 3 Control Channel Socket Arbitrary Command Execution Vulnerability
items.summary: A vulnerability in the control channel socket implementation of Open Source Snort 3 could allow an authenticated, local attacker with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands as the Snort 3 process user. This vulnerability is due to a lack of authentication when a local user connects to the Snort control channel socket. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the Snort 3 control channel socket as a local user. items.summary: A vulnerability in the interprocess communication (IPC) channel of the Secure Firewall Posture module in Cisco Secure Client could allow an authenticated, local attacker to elevate privileges on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a series of crafted IPC messages to a local socket. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to perform limited file write operations on the filesystem with SYSTEM or root privileges. items.title: Cisco Meraki Security Hardening Release: October 2026
items.summary: As part of Cisco's ongoing commitment to proactive security and product quality, engineering teams conducted a comprehensive internal security review. This review resulted in software hardening releases that address multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities were found during internal testing and are not known to be actively exploited. To assist customers in patching and streamline the disclosure process, Cisco has grouped these issues by their underlying vulnerability class — Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) — and assigned a single Common Vulnerabilitie

Cisco Secure Email Gateway Arbitrary File Write Vulnerability
items.summary: A vulnerability in the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system. This vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with  root privileges on the underlying operating system.

items.title: September 2026 Security Update
items.summary: Ivanti releases standard security patches on the second Tuesday of every month. In today’s rapidly evolving technology and threat landscape, we believe responsible transparency should be a cornerstone of any product security program. AI is compressing the time-to-exploit , and Ivanti uses leading technologies to proactively find and fix issues––including integrating advanced LLMs into our Engineering and product security to enhance the capabilities of our teams and identify vulnerabilities that traditional tools have previously missed. Our philosophy is simple: discovering and communicating vu

items.title: HTTP/2 Bomb CVE-2026-49975
items.summary: CVSSv3 Score: 5.8 CVE-2026-49975Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http leads to denial of service via malicious HTTP requests. This issue affects Apache HTTP Server: from 2.4.17 through 2.4.67. Revised on 2026-08-19 00:00:00

items.title: Broken access control in the RADIUS type admin group
items.summary: CVSSv3 Score: 9.8 An Improper Authentication vulnerability [CWE-287] in the FortiWeb Remote Radius Type Admin Authentication configured with specific, non-default settings may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to login into the Fortiweb GUI/CLI with a random username and password Revised on 2026-08-12 00:00:00

items.title: Content-Encoding WAF Evasion
items.summary: CVSSv3 Score: 5.3 An incomplete list of disallowed inputs [CWE-184] in FortiWeb WAF may allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass policies via specifically crafted requests. Revised on 2026-08-12 00:00:00

items.title: FGFM Authentication Weakening via CLI Configuration
items.summary: CVSSv3 Score: 8.1 An Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel [CWE-288] vulnerability in FortiManager and FortiManager Cloud may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to impersonate any FortiGate managed by the FortiManager with a specific CLI option set via crafted FGFM requests if the attacker has a valid certificate. Revised on 2026-08-12 00:00:00

items.title: Heap overflow in kernel driver due to missing size validation
items.summary: CVSSv3 Score: 7.3 A buffer copy without checking size of input vulnerability [CWE-120] in FortiClient Windows may allow an unauthenticated attacker in a position to alter or craft DNS responses to the targeted host to execute arbitrary code via malicious packets. Revised on 2026-08-12 00:00:00

items.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
items.summary: CVSSv3 Score: 3.8 A Server-Side request forgery (SSRF) [CWE-918] vulnerability in FortiSIEM GUI may allow an authenticated attacker to send HTTP requests originating from the targeted device via specially crafted HTTP requests Revised on 2026-08-12 00:00:00

items.title: Stack buffer overflow in WAD
items.summary: CVSSv3 Score: 5.6 A Stack-based Buffer Overflow vulnerability [CWE-121] in FortiOS explicit proxy may allow an unauthenticated attacker who can bypass stack protection and ASLR to execute arbitrary code or commands in the context of the WAD daemon via crafted sockets, only if the explicit proxy is configured with Kerberos authentication and SOCKS enabled. Revised on 2026-08-12 00:00:00

items.title: UI DoS attack
items.summary: CVSSv3 Score: 5.0 An Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability [CWE-770] in FortiOS may allow an unauthenticated attacker to perform a slow HTTP DoS attack on the web interface via crafted HTTP requests. Revised on 2026-08-12 00:00:00
